title.en: 3.1 Components, Icons, Dropdowns, Cards, Button and Input Groups

body.en:
A Bootstrap component is a ready-made, reusable user interface (UI) part, such as a navbar, card, dropdown, alert or progress bar. It is made of HTML with predefined Bootstrap classes. Interactive components also use Bootstrap's JavaScript (bootstrap.bundle.min.js).

Advantages of components

  • Saves time: no need to write CSS or JavaScript from scratch; just add classes.
  • Consistent look: all pages and buttons look the same across the website.
  • Responsive: components adjust automatically to phone, tablet and desktop.
  • Cross-browser: tested on all modern browsers.
  • Accessible: they use ARIA attributes and keyboard support for screen readers.
  • Easy to customise: colours, sizes and spacing are changed with utility classes or Sass variables.
  • Well documented with many examples, and a large community.

Types of components

TypeComponents
NavigationNavs (tabs, pills), navbar, breadcrumb, pagination, dropdown
Content containersCard (panel, thumbnail, well), list group, media object, jumbotron, accordion
Buttons and formsButtons, button group, button toolbar, input group, close button
Feedback / statusAlerts, badges (labels), progress bars, spinners, toasts
Overlays (Unit 4)Modal, tooltip, popover, offcanvas

CSS-only components (card, badge, breadcrumb, list group) need only bootstrap.css. JavaScript components (dropdown, navbar toggler, tabs, dismissible alert) also need bootstrap.bundle.min.js and work through data-bs-* attributes.

h.en: Bootstrap 3 Components and their Bootstrap 5 Replacements

body.en:
The GTU syllabus uses some Bootstrap 3 component names. Bootstrap 4 and 5 removed or renamed many of them. In this course we use Bootstrap 5, but you should know both names for the viva.

Bootstrap 3Bootstrap 5
Glyphicons (icon font in bootstrap.css)Bootstrap Icons, a separate library: bi bi-*
.label .label-danger.badge .bg-danger
.panel, .panel-heading, .panel-body.card, .card-header, .card-body
.thumbnail.card or .img-thumbnail
.well.card or .bg-light .p-3 .border
.jumbotronRemoved; use utilities .p-5 .bg-body-tertiary .rounded-3
.page-headerRemoved; use .border-bottom .pb-2 .mb-3
.media (BS3/BS4)Flex utilities: .d-flex .flex-shrink-0 .ms-3
.navbar-default / .navbar-inverse.bg-* with data-bs-theme="light" / "dark"
.pull-left / .pull-right.float-start / .float-end, or .ms-auto in flex
<span class="caret">Added automatically by .dropdown-toggle
data-toggle, data-targetdata-bs-toggle, data-bs-target
.input-group-addon.input-group-text

Reason for the changes: Bootstrap 4/5 moved to flexbox, removed jQuery, and made smaller general utility classes, so many single-purpose components were no longer needed.

Glyphicons were the icon font included in Bootstrap 3 (about 250 icons). Icons were added with a span: <span class="glyphicon glyphicon-search"></span>. Bootstrap 4 dropped Glyphicons.

Bootstrap Icons is the official free icon library for Bootstrap 5, with more than 2000 icons. It is a separate CSS + font file.

<!-- Bootstrap 3 -->
<span class="glyphicon glyphicon-user"></span>
<!-- Bootstrap 5 -->
<i class="bi bi-person"></i>

Using Bootstrap Icons

  1. Link bootstrap-icons.css in the head (from a CDN or a local copy).
  2. Add <i class="bi bi-{name}"></i> where the icon should appear.
  3. Because an icon is a font character, change its size with font-size (fs-1 to fs-6) and its colour with text colour classes (text-danger).
<!-- in <head> -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="bootstrap-icons.css">

<i class="bi bi-house"></i> Home
<i class="bi bi-search text-primary fs-4"></i>
<button class="btn btn-success">
  <i class="bi bi-download"></i> Download
</button>
<i class="bi bi-star-fill" style="color: orange"></i>

Common icons

  • bi-house, bi-person, bi-envelope, bi-telephone, bi-search
  • bi-cart, bi-heart, bi-star-fill, bi-trash, bi-pencil, bi-download
  • bi-list (menu), bi-x-lg (close), bi-check-circle, bi-exclamation-triangle

Icons are used in buttons, navbars, menus, alerts and list items. For accessibility, add aria-hidden="true" to decorative icons, or a visually-hidden text label for icon-only buttons.

A dropdown is a toggleable menu that shows a list of links when a button or link is clicked. It is a JavaScript component and needs bootstrap.bundle.min.js (which includes Popper.js for positioning).

Structure

  • Wrapper .dropdown (or .btn-group).
  • Toggle button with .dropdown-toggle and data-bs-toggle="dropdown"; the caret is added automatically.
  • Menu ul.dropdown-menu with a.dropdown-item items.
<div class="dropdown">
  <button class="btn btn-primary dropdown-toggle"
      type="button" data-bs-toggle="dropdown">
    Courses
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu">
    <li><h6 class="dropdown-header">Diploma</h6></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">Computer</a></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item active" href="#">IT</a></li>
    <li><hr class="dropdown-divider"></li>
    <li><a class="dropdown-item disabled">M.E.</a></li>
  </ul>
</div>

Menu options

ClassUse
.dropdown-headerNon-clickable heading inside the menu
.dropdown-dividerHorizontal line between groups (BS3: li.divider)
.active / .disabledHighlighted current item / greyed-out item
.dropdown-item-textPlain text item
.dropdown-menu-endMenu aligned to the right edge
.dropdown-menu-darkDark menu
.dropup / .dropend / .dropstartMenu opens upward / right / left
.dropdown-toggle-splitSplit button: action part + caret part
<div class="btn-group">
  <button class="btn btn-danger">Action</button>
  <button class="btn btn-danger dropdown-toggle
      dropdown-toggle-split" data-bs-toggle="dropdown">
  </button>
  <ul class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-end">...</ul>
</div>
<div class="btn-group dropup">...</div>

Events: show.bs.dropdown, shown.bs.dropdown, hide.bs.dropdown, hidden.bs.dropdown. Forms can also be placed inside a dropdown menu.

A card is a flexible content container with optional header, footer, image and body. In Bootstrap 4/5, the card replaced the BS3 panel, well and thumbnail.

Parts of a card

  • .card: outer box with border and rounded corners.
  • .card-header / .card-footer: grey strips at the top and bottom.
  • .card-body: padded content area containing .card-title, .card-subtitle, .card-text and .card-link.
  • .card-img-top / .card-img-bottom: full-width image at the top or bottom.
  • .card-img-overlay: places text on top of the image.
<div class="card" style="width: 18rem">
  <img src="course.jpg" class="card-img-top" alt="Course">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h5 class="card-title">Python Course</h5>
    <p class="card-text">Learn Python in 30 days.</p>
    <a href="#" class="btn btn-primary">Enroll</a>
  </div>
  <div class="card-footer text-muted">Starts 1 Dec</div>
</div>

Card layouts and styles

  • Grid of cards: cards inside grid columns; .h-100 gives equal height.
  • .card-group: joined cards of equal height.
  • Horizontal card: a row inside the card with image in col-md-4 and body in col-md-8.
  • Colours: text-bg-primary, border-success.
  • List group in card: ul.list-group.list-group-flush.
  • Width: 100% by default; set it with the grid, w-* utilities or a style.
<div class="row row-cols-1 row-cols-md-3 g-3">
  <div class="col">
    <div class="card h-100">...</div>
  </div>
  <div class="col">
    <div class="card h-100 text-bg-success">...</div>
  </div>
</div>

A button group joins several buttons together in a single line (no gap, only the outer corners rounded). A button toolbar combines several button groups in one row.

Button group

<div class="btn-group" role="group">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Left</button>
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Middle</button>
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Right</button>
</div>
<div class="btn-group-vertical">...</div>
  • .btn-group: horizontal group. Add role="group" and an aria-label for accessibility.
  • .btn-group-vertical: buttons stacked vertically.
  • Sizes: .btn-group-lg, .btn-group-sm on the group instead of on every button.
  • Toggle group: radio or checkbox inputs with .btn-check and labels with .btn, so one or more buttons stay selected.

Button toolbar

<div class="btn-toolbar" role="toolbar">
  <div class="btn-group me-2">
    <button class="btn btn-secondary">1</button>
    <button class="btn btn-secondary">2</button>
  </div>
  <div class="btn-group">
    <button class="btn btn-info">8</button>
  </div>
</div>

Use spacing utilities (me-2) between the groups. Input groups can also be placed in a toolbar.

Nesting (dropdown inside a group)

Place a .btn-group containing a dropdown inside another .btn-group. This creates a group where one button opens a submenu, e.g. odd and even semester buttons with subject menus.

<div class="btn-group">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Sem 1</button>
  <div class="btn-group">
    <button class="btn btn-primary dropdown-toggle"
        data-bs-toggle="dropdown">Sem 3</button>
    <ul class="dropdown-menu">
      <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="#">RWPD</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

Uses: pagination-like controls, text editor toolbars (bold, italic, underline), view switchers (list/grid), semester selectors.

An input group extends a form control by adding text, icons or buttons before, after or on both sides of the input in one joined box.

<div class="input-group mb-3">
  <span class="input-group-text">@</span>
  <input type="text" class="form-control"
      placeholder="Username">
</div>
<div class="input-group mb-3">
  <span class="input-group-text">Rs.</span>
  <input type="number" class="form-control">
  <span class="input-group-text">.00</span>
</div>
<div class="input-group">
  <input type="text" class="form-control"
      placeholder="Search">
  <button class="btn btn-primary">Go</button>
</div>

Classes and options

  • .input-group: wrapper; its children are joined together.
  • .input-group-text: grey add-on with text or an icon (BS3: .input-group-addon).
  • Buttons and dropdowns can be added directly as add-ons.
  • Checkbox or radio inside .input-group-text with .form-check-input.
  • Multiple inputs (e.g. first and last name) and multiple add-ons are allowed.
  • Select and file input: .form-select, input type="file".
  • Sizes: .input-group-sm, .input-group-lg.
  • .flex-nowrap stops the parts wrapping onto a new line on small screens.

Examples: @ for username, +91 for mobile, Rs. and .00 for an amount, envelope icon for email, Search + Go button, "https://" before a website field.

Always connect a label (or aria-label) with the input because the add-on text is not a label.

title.en: 3.2 Navs, Navbar, Breadcrumb, Pagination and Badges

body.en:
Navs are navigation components built from a list of links. The base class .nav with .nav-item and .nav-link gives a simple horizontal menu.

<ul class="nav nav-tabs">
  <li class="nav-item">
    <a class="nav-link active" href="#">Unit 1</a>
  </li>
  <li class="nav-item">
    <a class="nav-link" href="#">Unit 2</a>
  </li>
  <li class="nav-item">
    <a class="nav-link disabled">Unit 3</a>
  </li>
</ul>
<!-- pills: nav nav-pills, vertical: add flex-column -->

Nav styles

ClassResult
.nav-tabsTabs: the active link looks like a folder tab joined to the content below
.nav-pillsPills: the active link has a coloured rounded background
.nav-underlineActive link underlined
.nav-fill / .nav-justifiedItems fill the full width (justified = equal widths)
.flex-columnVertical (stacked) nav
.justify-content-center / -endCentre or right-align the items
.active / .disabledCurrent item / disabled item

Tab and pill plug-in (dynamic tabs)

With JavaScript, tabs and pills switch between content panes without loading a new page.

  • Each link gets data-bs-toggle="tab" (or "pill") and data-bs-target="#id".
  • Panes are .tab-pane inside .tab-content; the first pane has show active.
  • .fade gives a fade animation.
<ul class="nav nav-tabs" role="tablist">
  <li class="nav-item">
    <button class="nav-link active" data-bs-toggle="tab"
        data-bs-target="#u1" type="button">Unit 1</button>
  </li>
  <li class="nav-item">
    <button class="nav-link" data-bs-toggle="tab"
        data-bs-target="#u2" type="button">Unit 2</button>
  </li>
</ul>
<div class="tab-content p-3 border border-top-0">
  <div class="tab-pane fade show active" id="u1">
    Introduction...</div>
  <div class="tab-pane fade" id="u2">Grid...</div>
</div>

Events: show.bs.tab, shown.bs.tab, hide.bs.tab. From code: bootstrap.Tab.getOrCreateInstance(el).show().

A navbar is the responsive navigation header of a website. It contains the brand (logo/name), navigation links, dropdowns, forms and buttons. On small screens it collapses behind a hamburger (toggler) button.

<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-lg bg-dark"
    data-bs-theme="dark">
  <div class="container-fluid">
    <a class="navbar-brand" href="#">DiplomaOne</a>
    <button class="navbar-toggler" type="button"
        data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#menu">
      <span class="navbar-toggler-icon"></span>
    </button>
    <div class="collapse navbar-collapse" id="menu">
      <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
        <li class="nav-item">
          <a class="nav-link active" href="#">Home</a>
        </li>
        <li class="nav-item">
          <a class="nav-link" href="#">About</a>
        </li>
      </ul>
      <form class="d-flex">
        <input class="form-control me-2" type="search">
        <button class="btn btn-warning">Search</button>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</nav>

Parts of a navbar

  • .navbar with .navbar-expand-{bp}: the menu is expanded from that breakpoint upward and collapsed below it (e.g. lg = collapsed below 992 px).
  • .navbar-brand: website name or logo image.
  • .navbar-toggler with .navbar-toggler-icon: the hamburger button; data-bs-toggle="collapse" opens the menu.
  • .collapse.navbar-collapse: the part that is hidden on small screens; its id matches data-bs-target.
  • .navbar-nav with .nav-item / .nav-link: the links; .dropdown items are allowed.
  • .navbar-text: plain text.
  • Forms: form.d-flex for a search box; me-auto on navbar-nav pushes the form to the right.

Colour schemes

Use a background class (bg-dark, bg-primary, bg-body-tertiary) and data-bs-theme="dark" for light text. (BS3: .navbar-default and .navbar-inverse.)

Fixed navbar

ClassBehaviour
.fixed-topStays at the top of the screen while scrolling
.fixed-bottomStays at the bottom (used for footers)
.sticky-topScrolls with the page, then sticks at the top

Fixed elements are removed from the normal flow, so add padding-top (and padding-bottom) to the body so that content is not hidden behind them.

<nav class="navbar fixed-top bg-primary">...</nav>
<footer class="fixed-bottom bg-dark text-white">
  ...</footer>
<style>
  body { padding-top: 60px; padding-bottom: 50px; }
</style>

Breadcrumb

A breadcrumb shows the current page's location in the website hierarchy, e.g. Home / Computer / Sem 3 / RWPD. Each level is a link except the current page.

<nav aria-label="breadcrumb">
  <ol class="breadcrumb">
    <li class="breadcrumb-item"><a href="#">Home</a></li>
    <li class="breadcrumb-item"><a href="#">Sem 3</a></li>
    <li class="breadcrumb-item active">RWPD</li>
  </ol>
</nav>
  • ol.breadcrumb with li.breadcrumb-item; the last item has .active and aria-current="page".
  • The separator "/" is added by CSS. Change it with the CSS variable --bs-breadcrumb-divider, e.g. '>'.
  • Wrap it in nav aria-label="breadcrumb" for accessibility.

Pagination

Pagination splits long content (search results, products, articles) into pages and shows numbered page links.

<ul class="pagination justify-content-center">
  <li class="page-item disabled">
    <a class="page-link">Previous</a>
  </li>
  <li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#">1</a></li>
  <li class="page-item active">
    <a class="page-link" href="#">2</a>
  </li>
  <li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#">3</a></li>
  <li class="page-item"><a class="page-link" href="#">Next</a></li>
</ul>
  • Structure: ul.pagination > li.page-item > a.page-link.
  • .active marks the current page; .disabled greys out Previous on the first page or Next on the last page.
  • Sizes: .pagination-lg, .pagination-sm.
  • Alignment: justify-content-center or -end on the ul.
  • Arrows: use « and » (shown as double arrows) for Previous / Next.

With JavaScript: keep a list of items and show only the items of the current page: items.slice((page - 1) * perPage, page * perPage). Rebuild the page links on every click.

A badge is a small count or label that is attached to text, buttons or links, e.g. "New", the number of unread messages, or a status. In Bootstrap 3 these were called labels (.label .label-success) and badges (rounded counters); Bootstrap 5 joins both in .badge.

<h4>Notices <span class="badge bg-danger">New</span></h4>
<span class="badge rounded-pill text-bg-warning">Pill</span>
<button class="btn btn-primary">
  Inbox <span class="badge text-bg-light">7</span>
</button>
<button class="btn btn-dark position-relative">
  <i class="bi bi-bell"></i>
  <span class="position-absolute top-0 start-100
      translate-middle badge rounded-pill bg-danger">3</span>
</button>
  • Colour: bg-* or text-bg-* (text-bg also sets a readable text colour).
  • .rounded-pill: pill-shaped badge.
  • Size: a badge scales with its parent, so a badge in an h1 is larger than one in a paragraph.
  • In buttons: shows counts like Inbox 7.
  • Positioned: position-absolute top-0 start-100 translate-middle puts a notification count on the corner of an icon button.
  • Add visually-hidden text (e.g. "unread messages") so screen readers understand the number.

Uses: new items, notification counts, status (Paid / Pending), tags and categories, ratings in list groups.

title.en: 3.3 Jumbotron, Thumbnails, Alerts, Progress, Media, List Group and Panels

body.en:
Jumbotron

A jumbotron is a large, padded box with a light background used to highlight important content, such as the main message on a home page, with a big heading, a lead paragraph and a call-to-action button.

  • Bootstrap 3 and 4 had the class .jumbotron (and .jumbotron-fluid for full width).
  • Bootstrap 5 removed it; the same result is built with utilities: padding p-5, background bg-body-tertiary, rounded-3, big heading display-5, and lead text.
  • For a full-width jumbotron, put it outside the container and use a container inside.
<div class="p-5 mb-4 bg-body-tertiary rounded-3">
  <h1 class="display-5 fw-bold">Learn Web Design</h1>
  <p class="lead">Free notes for GTU diploma students.</p>
  <a class="btn btn-primary btn-lg" href="#">Get started</a>
</div>

Page header

A page header is a heading at the top of a page or section with extra space and a line below it. BS3 used .page-header; in BS5 use border-bottom pb-2 mb-3, with a small grey subtitle.

<div class="border-bottom pb-2 mb-3">
  <h1>Exam Results
    <small class="text-body-secondary">Summer 2026</small>
  </h1>
</div>

A thumbnail is a small preview image (often with a caption) shown in a grid, used for photo galleries, products, courses or videos.

  • Bootstrap 3: .thumbnail on a box around an image, with .caption for the text.
  • Bootstrap 5: .img-thumbnail gives an image a 1 px border, padding and rounded corners. For thumbnails with captions and buttons, use cards in grid columns.
<!-- simple bordered image -->
<img src="lab.jpg" class="img-thumbnail" alt="Lab">
<!-- BS3 .thumbnail with caption = BS5 card -->
<div class="col-md-4">
  <div class="card">
    <img src="lab.jpg" class="card-img-top" alt="Lab">
    <div class="card-body">
      <h5>Computer Lab</h5>
      <a href="#" class="btn btn-primary">View</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Thumbnail gallery steps

  1. Create a .row with g-3 gutters.
  2. Use responsive columns such as col-6 col-md-3 (2 per row on phones, 4 on desktop).
  3. In each column put an image with img-fluid img-thumbnail, or a card with card-img-top.
  4. Add a caption, and wrap the image in a link for a larger view.

The education site example (Practical 14) combines a breadcrumb, a jumbotron, badges, thumbnails and pagination on one page.

Alerts provide contextual feedback messages for user actions, e.g. success after saving, an error, a warning or information.

<div class="alert alert-success" role="alert">
  <strong>Saved!</strong> Your form was submitted.
</div>
<div class="alert alert-warning alert-dismissible fade show">
  Last date for fees is 30 Nov.
  <button type="button" class="btn-close"
      data-bs-dismiss="alert"></button>
</div>

Alert classes

  • .alert with a colour: alert-primary, -secondary, -success, -danger, -warning, -info, -light, -dark.
  • .alert-link: link in the matching colour; .alert-heading: title in the alert.
  • Dismissible alert: add .alert-dismissible and a close button button.btn-close data-bs-dismiss="alert". .fade .show adds a fade-out animation.
  • Add role="alert" so screen readers announce the message.

Alert JavaScript

The alert plug-in fires close.bs.alert (when closing starts) and closed.bs.alert (after it is removed). A message can be shown after an alert is closed, as in Practical 17.

var box = document.getElementById("fee");
box.addEventListener("closed.bs.alert", function () {
  msg.textContent = "Alert closed";
});
// close from code
bootstrap.Alert.getOrCreateInstance(box).close();

New alerts can be created by inserting alert HTML into a container with JavaScript.

A progress bar shows how much of a task is complete, e.g. a file upload, the steps of a form, course completion or skill levels.

<div class="progress" style="height: 20px">
  <div class="progress-bar bg-success" style="width: 75%">
    75%</div>
</div>
<div class="progress">
  <div class="progress-bar progress-bar-striped
      progress-bar-animated bg-danger" style="width: 85%">
  </div>
</div>

Types of progress bars

TypeHow
Basic.progress outer track + .progress-bar with style="width: 40%"
With labelText inside .progress-bar (e.g. 75%)
Heightstyle="height: 20px" on .progress
Colouredbg-success, bg-info, bg-warning, bg-danger
Striped.progress-bar-striped
Animated.progress-bar-striped .progress-bar-animated (stripes move)
Multiple (stacked)Several bars in .progress-stacked, each in its own .progress

For accessibility add role="progressbar" and aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax.

Changing progress with JavaScript

Change the width style and the text of the bar. setInterval() increases the value step by step.

var v = 0;
var t = setInterval(function () {
  v = v + 10;
  bar.style.width = v + "%";
  bar.textContent = v + "%";
  if (v >= 100) clearInterval(t);
}, 500);

A media object is a layout with an image (or video, icon) on one side and text content beside it. It is used for comments, tweets, blog posts, testimonials and profile lists.

  • Bootstrap 3/4: .media, .media-left, .media-body, .media-heading.
  • Bootstrap 5: the media component was removed because the same layout is made with flex utilities: .d-flex on the wrapper, .flex-shrink-0 on the image part, .flex-grow-1 .ms-3 on the text part.
<div class="d-flex">
  <div class="flex-shrink-0">
    <img src="grandpa.jpg" width="64" alt="">
  </div>
  <div class="flex-grow-1 ms-3">
    <h5>Grandfather</h5>
    Retired teacher.
    <div class="d-flex mt-3">  <!-- nested -->
      <img src="father.jpg" width="48" alt="">
      <div class="ms-3"><h6>Father</h6>Engineer.</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Variations

  • Nesting: place another d-flex block inside the text part, e.g. replies to a comment or a family tree (Practical 16).
  • Alignment: align-items-center or align-self-end moves the image to the middle or bottom.
  • Order: put the image after the text (with ms-3) for a right-aligned image.
  • Media list: use a ul with list-unstyled and each li as a d-flex media item.

List group

A list group displays a series of content items as a bordered list. It is used for menus, settings, notifications and lists of providers.

<ul class="list-group">
  <li class="list-group-item active">JioFiber</li>
  <li class="list-group-item d-flex
      justify-content-between">Airtel
    <span class="badge bg-primary rounded-pill">4.3</span>
  </li>
  <li class="list-group-item disabled">BSNL</li>
  <li class="list-group-item list-group-item-success">
    DGVCL</li>
</ul>
<div class="list-group">
  <a href="#" class="list-group-item
      list-group-item-action">Clickable item</a>
</div>
  • ul.list-group with li.list-group-item.
  • .active / .disabled: current or disabled item.
  • Links and buttons: div.list-group with a.list-group-item-action for hover and click effects.
  • Colours: list-group-item-success, -danger, -warning, etc.
  • .list-group-flush: removes outer borders (used inside cards); .list-group-numbered: numbers the items; .list-group-horizontal: items in a row.
  • Badges with d-flex justify-content-between show counts on the right.
  • With data-bs-toggle="list", list items work like tabs.

Panels

A panel (Bootstrap 3) is a bordered box with a coloured heading and a body, used to group related content, e.g. "Internet providers". Classes: .panel .panel-primary, .panel-heading, .panel-title, .panel-body, .panel-footer. Panels were replaced by cards in Bootstrap 4/5.

<!-- BS3 panel -->
<div class="panel panel-primary">
  <div class="panel-heading">Internet</div>
  <div class="panel-body">...</div>
</div>
<!-- BS5 equivalent -->
<div class="card border-primary">
  <div class="card-header text-bg-primary">Internet</div>
  <div class="card-body">...</div>
</div>

Practical 17 combines card panels, list groups and dismissible alerts, and shows a message after an alert is closed.

q.en: What is a Bootstrap component?

a.en: A ready-made, reusable UI part (navbar, card, alert, dropdown ...) built with HTML and Bootstrap classes, plus JavaScript for interactive ones.

q.en: Give four advantages of Bootstrap components.

a.en: They save time, give a consistent look, are responsive, work in all browsers, are accessible and easy to customise.

q.en: Name the types of Bootstrap components.

a.en: Navigation (navs, navbar, breadcrumb, pagination), content (card, list group, media), buttons and forms (button group, input group), feedback (alert, badge, progress).

q.en: Which file is needed for JavaScript components?

a.en: bootstrap.bundle.min.js, which includes Popper.js.

q.en: What are Glyphicons?

a.en: The icon font included in Bootstrap 3 (about 250 icons), used as span.glyphicon.glyphicon-name.

q.en: What replaced Glyphicons in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: Bootstrap Icons, a separate free library used as i.bi.bi-name.

q.en: How do you change the size and colour of a Bootstrap icon?

a.en: It is a font, so use font-size (fs-1 to fs-6) and text colour classes such as text-danger.

q.en: Which attribute opens a dropdown?

a.en: data-bs-toggle="dropdown" on the toggle button.

q.en: What does .dropdown-toggle do?

a.en: Marks the toggle button and adds the caret automatically.

q.en: What is .dropdown-header?

a.en: A non-clickable heading inside a dropdown menu.

q.en: What is .dropdown-divider?

a.en: A horizontal line that separates groups of items.

q.en: How do you make a dropdown open upward?

a.en: Use .dropup instead of .dropdown (.dropend and .dropstart for right and left).

q.en: What is a split button dropdown?

a.en: A button group with an action button and a separate caret button with .dropdown-toggle-split.

q.en: What is a card?

a.en: A flexible content container with optional header, image, body and footer.

q.en: Which Bootstrap 3 components were replaced by the card?

a.en: Panel, well and thumbnail.

q.en: Name the parts of a card body.

a.en: .card-title, .card-subtitle, .card-text and .card-link.

q.en: How do you make cards in a row the same height?

a.en: Put them in grid columns and add .h-100 to each card (or use .card-group).

q.en: What is a button group?

a.en: A set of buttons joined in one line using .btn-group.

q.en: What is a button toolbar?

a.en: A .btn-toolbar that contains several button groups in a row.

q.en: How do you make a vertical button group?

a.en: Use .btn-group-vertical.

q.en: How do you add a dropdown inside a button group?

a.en: Nest a .btn-group containing the dropdown toggle and menu inside the main .btn-group.

q.en: What is an input group?

a.en: A form control with text, icons or buttons added before or after it in one joined box.

q.en: Which class holds the add-on text in an input group?

a.en: .input-group-text (Bootstrap 3: .input-group-addon).

q.en: How do you change the size of an input group?

a.en: Add .input-group-sm or .input-group-lg to the wrapper.

q.en: Difference between nav tabs and nav pills?

a.en: Tabs look like folder tabs joined to the content; pills show the active link with a coloured rounded background.

q.en: How do you make a vertical nav?

a.en: Add .flex-column to the .nav.

q.en: What is the difference between .nav-fill and .nav-justified?

a.en: .nav-fill fills the width with items of different widths; .nav-justified gives all items equal width.

q.en: How do tabs switch content without reloading the page?

a.en: data-bs-toggle="tab" and data-bs-target link each tab to a .tab-pane inside .tab-content.

q.en: What is a navbar?

a.en: A responsive navigation header with brand, links, dropdowns and forms that collapses on small screens.

q.en: What does .navbar-expand-lg mean?

a.en: The menu is expanded from the lg breakpoint (992 px) and collapsed behind the toggler below it.

q.en: What is .navbar-toggler?

a.en: The hamburger button that opens and closes the collapsed menu.

q.en: How do you make a fixed navbar?

a.en: Add .fixed-top (or .fixed-bottom) and add body padding so content is not hidden.

q.en: Difference between .fixed-top and .sticky-top?

a.en: .fixed-top is always fixed; .sticky-top scrolls with the page until it reaches the top, then sticks.

q.en: How is a dark navbar made in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: bg-dark with data-bs-theme="dark" (Bootstrap 3: .navbar-inverse).

q.en: What is a breadcrumb?

a.en: A navigation aid showing the current page's location in the site hierarchy, e.g. Home / Sem 3 / RWPD.

q.en: What is pagination?

a.en: Numbered page links that split long content into pages: ul.pagination > li.page-item > a.page-link.

q.en: What is a badge?

a.en: A small label or count attached to text or buttons, e.g. New or 7 unread.

q.en: What were labels in Bootstrap 3 called in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: Badges (.label became .badge).

q.en: What is a jumbotron?

a.en: A large padded box with a light background used to highlight the main message of a page.

q.en: Is .jumbotron available in Bootstrap 5?

a.en: No. It is built with utilities like p-5, bg-body-tertiary, rounded-3 and display-5.

q.en: What is .img-thumbnail?

a.en: An image class that adds padding, a 1 px border and rounded corners.

q.en: What is an alert?

a.en: A contextual feedback message, e.g. success, danger, warning or info.

q.en: How do you make a dismissible alert?

a.en: Add .alert-dismissible and a button.btn-close with data-bs-dismiss="alert"; .fade .show animate it.

q.en: Which event fires after an alert is closed?

a.en: closed.bs.alert (close.bs.alert fires when closing starts).

q.en: What is a progress bar?

a.en: A bar showing how much of a task is complete: .progress with a .progress-bar whose width is set in %.

q.en: How do you make an animated progress bar?

a.en: Add .progress-bar-striped and .progress-bar-animated.

q.en: How do you change a progress bar with JavaScript?

a.en: Set bar.style.width = value + "%" and update its text.

q.en: What is a media object?

a.en: An image on one side with text beside it; in Bootstrap 5 it is made with d-flex, flex-shrink-0 and ms-3.

q.en: What is a list group?

a.en: A bordered list of items: .list-group with .list-group-item.

q.en: What does .list-group-item-action do?

a.en: Adds hover and active effects to clickable list items (links or buttons).

q.en: What is a panel?

a.en: A Bootstrap 3 bordered box with a coloured heading and body, replaced by cards in Bootstrap 4/5.
